title: Pinch-pot heart-shaped dish in air-dry clay
subtitle: A small trinket or ring dish formed by pinching a heart outline
excerpt: A flat heart-shaped dish pinched from a single ball of air-dry clay. The sides are raised just enough to hold rings or small jewellery items. No kiln is needed: the piece dries at room temperature in a day and can be painted or left natural.
sourceNotes: Technique derived from first principles. Pinch-building methods referenced from Encyclopedia Britannica 11th edition (1911) pottery entry.

glossaryTerms.definition: A clay form opened and shaped by pressing the thumb into the centre of a ball and pinching the walls outward between thumb and fingers
The drying stage where clay holds its shape but is still firm enough to refine without distorting
Fully air-dried and unfired; fragile, ready for surface sealing

content.text: A
pinch pot

opened flat and shaped into a heart makes one of the simplest useful objects in clay. The walls stand 1 to 2 cm high to contain rings or earrings. No kiln is required, and the whole piece can be formed in 15 minutes, leaving the rest of the day to drying.
Forming
Roll 80 g of clay into a smooth ball. Press the thumb of your dominant hand into the centre until it is about 1 cm from the base.

Pinch the wall between thumb inside and two fingers outside, rotating the ball a quarter-turn between each pinch. Work the wall to an even 6 mm thickness. The bowl should be around 9 cm across at this stage.
Place the bowl right-way-up on the work surface and press it gently down into a flat-bottomed dish shape with the palm. The walls should rise about 1.5 cm from the base.

Pinch the rim at the top to create the two lobes of the heart shape: squeeze the two top points together to form the central dip of the V, and pinch the bottom of the bowl to a single downward point. Work slowly, pulling clay rather than compressing it.
Smooth the inner and outer surfaces with a barely damp sponge. Use the needle tool to refine the V notch and the bottom point. A wooden rib smoothed around the outer wall gives a cleaner finish.
Drying
Set the dish on a flat surface to dry at room temperature. It reaches
leather-hard
in 3 to 4 hours, at which point any uneven rim edges can be sanded lightly with fine sandpaper. Full
bone-dry
takes 18 to 24 hours for a piece this small.
Finishing

Apply two coats of diluted PVA to the whole dish. When dry, decorate with acrylic paint: a solid colour, marbled effect using two colours swirled together while wet, or a simple hand-lettered word or initial pressed with a needle tool before the clay dried. Gold or copper paint on the rim edge alone gives a clean decorative result.
Use and care
Suitable for jewellery and small items on a dressing table. Not food-safe or waterproof. Keep away from moisture.
Variations
Make three nested sizes using 60 g, 80 g, and 120 g clay balls for a set of graduated dishes.
Press a flower or leaf stamp into the base of the dish before drying to create a textured floor.
Troubleshooter

items.problem: The V notch of the heart closes back up during drying
items.cause: Clay elastic memory causes the pinched indent to relax as it dries
items.fix: Insert a small wedge of folded paper into the V notch while the clay is leather-hard to hold the shape open. Remove before bone-dry

items.problem: Rim cracks at the heart points
items.cause: The thin pinched points dry faster than the body and pull apart
items.fix: Cover the dish with a loose cloth for the first few hours to slow drying. At leather-hard, smooth the crack with a damp finger and allow to dry slowly

items.problem: Base is thinner in the centre than at the edges
items.cause: Uneven pinching has drawn clay from the base into the walls
items.fix: Press the base flat onto the work surface gently before drying. If very thin, add a thin coil of soft clay to the underside of the base and smooth it in before the piece dries
